surfaces.part: sign box head (white panel with teal symbol)
shaft with teal header band, yellow '4' panel and gray lower panel

answer.evidence: The head is rows 0-9 and widens from 10 to 12 to 14 at the top corners, then ends flat at row 9 with a 2px neck at row 10. That is a hat shape, not an ellipse plate. The white area (rows 1-7) has the teal symbol centered in it, so it reads as a face-on sign panel and not a horizontal surface. Row 8 is only a darker bottom edge, and there is no eave shadow below it. The shaft (rows 11-29, width 10) is a flat vertical face: a teal band, a yellow panel with the '4', and a gray lower panel. No part of the object shows an elliptical overhanging cap or a top surface, so it is a front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small pillar sign with a white cap and a yellow panel carrying the number 4. It measures 13 visible tones per tile, which is above bus-shelter-a (6) and kiosk-a (12) and below vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 9%, equal to bus-shelter-a and above the 0% of kiosk-a and vending-a. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted with a dark blue-grey material tone rather than a black sticker line, matching the references. The body has about 4 steps of shading (dark body, mid, highlight edge, cap light). The references run 5-6 steps and carry more texture. Vending-a has more varied detail in the panels and kiosk-a has stripes and grain. The candidate reads as a clean, simple prop with limited grain on the pole body and little texture, so it sits a bit below the richer references. It would sit acceptably beside bus-shelter-a but looks slightly thinner than kiosk-a and vending-a.
